This is a BC buyer FAQ utility page, not an area page and not a listing feed: headed "FAQ for Home Buyers in BC (2026) | Subjects, Costs & Programs," it bills itself as "16 Questions Answered · Updated 2026" and is built as five themed sections — The Offer & Subjects; Money & Financing; Closing & Costs; Taxes; Working With a REALTOR® — followed by a structured FAQ block of eight Q&A pairs (subjects; subject removal; deposit on collapse; down payment; deposit vs. down payment; GST; PTT; pre-approval).

items.t: Scope: buyers anywhere in British Columbia — first-time or repeat — pricing subjects, deposits, closing costs and taxes before writing an offer. There are no streets, edges or sub-area boundaries for this page, and no condo stock "concentrates" anywhere for it.

What the page's "stock" is: any BC home purchase — resale homes (subjects, PTT), new builds and presales (GST and the federal rebates), and strata purchases (strata-document subjects) — worked through subjects, money, closing, taxes and representation.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in FAQ for Home Buyers in BC

items.t: GST — FTHB GST/HST Rebate (verified, CRA): Bill C-4 received Royal Assent on March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 (secondary sources saying March 12 are superseded; CRA governs); together with the GST/HST new housing rebate it provides 100% of the GST (or federal part of the HST) on a newly constructed or substantially renovated home valued up to $1 million, is gradually reduced between $1 million and $1.5 million, and is not available at $1.5 million or more — a maximum of up to $50,000, for agreements March 20, 2025–2031. 5% GST applies to newly built and presale homes and not to resale homes, as the page states.

GST New Housing Rebate (verified, CRA): generally 36% of the GST paid, to a maximum rebate of $6,300, gradually reduced for homes priced or valued between $350,000 and $450,000, and not available at $450,000 or more. The live FAQ page does not state the old rebate's own numbers; they are recorded here so the rebuild can add them accurately.

Property Transfer Tax (verified, Province): 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million, 3% above $2 million, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3 million; the tax is based on fair market value on the day of registration at the Land Title Office, and PTT cannot be blended into the mortgage, as the page correctly notes. Newly Built Home Exemption (standard block): full to $1,100,000, partial to $1,150,000.

Down payment and mortgage insurance (verified, CMHC): mortgage loan insurance is required when a down payment is less than 20% of the purchase price; the minimum down payment is 5% for homes $500,000 or less, 5% on the first $500,000 plus 10% on the portion over $500,000 for homes between $500,000 and $1,499,999, and 20% at $1,500,000 or more (where insurance is not available); CMHC's published premium range is 0.6% to 4.5% of the total mortgage amount. The page's down-payment tiers and its $750,000 worked example ($25,000 + $25,000 = $50,000 minimum) match the verified tiers.

HBP / FHSA — standard-block figures with the research position attached: What IS verified is that the CRA states a person can make a qualifying FHSA withdrawal and also withdraw under the Home Buyers' Plan for the same qualifying home, as long as all conditions are met at the time of each withdrawal. Confirm both limits with the CRA or a lender before planning around them.

Practice norms — page statements only, not confirmed as stated norms: a deposit "typically around 5% of the purchase price" due upon or within 24 hours of subject removal; a typical subject period of 7 days (5 business days plus the weekend); a home inspection fee of $400–$700; closing costs of 1.5%–4% of the purchase price as a rule of thumb; pre-approval rate holds of 90–120 days and a 1–2 week pre-approval process; and completion "commonly 2–3 months" after acceptance. Each is practitioner copy, negotiable or market-dependent in fact, with no official source opened.

Representation — page framing only: the page states buyers typically pay no direct commission (the seller's listing contract carries a gross commission split between the agents), that dual agency is banned in BC except in very limited circumstances, and that an unrepresented buyer is a "customer" to whom the listing agent owes no fiduciary duty.

Pad rent (parks): no park tenancy is part of this FAQ page; where a purchase is a manufactured home on a rented pad, the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act governs, with pad-rent limits of 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026 and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027 — never publish a pad-rent dollar figure, and none is published here.

items.t: The page never states the old rebate's own numbers — but they are now verified.
The page's PTT wording checks out — including its "up to $8,000" saving.
This is the one buyer page without the CMHC range error.

Two rescission clocks share one page's vocabulary. The FAQ's rescission answer concerns accepted offers generally (3 business days, 0.25% — not confirmed as stated), while a presale developer contract carries REDMA's separate 7-day rescission under s. 21 with deposits in trust under s. 18 — a buyer who merges the two clocks misprices the risk of a subject-free resale offer.

The $750,000 example is the page's one fully checkable calculation. Input $750,000 under the verified CMHC tiers: $25,000 (5% of the first $500,000) plus $25,000 (10% of the $250,000 balance) equals a $50,000 minimum down payment — the page's arithmetic matches the verified tiers exactly.
The typical reader is checking three numbers before a first offer.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in FAQ for Home Buyers in BC

items.t: New Housing Rebate: generally 36% of the GST paid, maximum $6,300, gradually reduced for homes priced or valued between $350,000 and $450,000, not available at $450,000 or more. The live FAQ page does not state the old rebate's own numbers; they are recorded here so the rebuild can add them accurately.

: minimum down payment 5% for homes $500,000 or less; 5% on the first $500,000 plus 10% on the portion over $500,000 for homes between $500,000 and $1,499,999; 20% at $1,500,000 or more, where insurance is not available; mortgage loan insurance is required below 20% down, and CMHC's published premium range is 0.6% to 4.5% of the total mortgage amount. The page's tiers and its $750,000 worked example ($25,000 + $25,000 = $50,000 minimum) match the verified tiers.

Strata block (bare-land strata lots, where a purchase takes that form): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF since November 1, 2023; rental bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A fee-simple lot carries none of this.

ALR block (where a reader's parcel is ALR — status per-parcel, not verified here): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

items.t: The header count is the one open rendered-page item (Nov 1, 2026).

The live FAQ states the new FTHB rebate but not the pre-existing new housing rebate's own figures (36%, maximum $6,300, $350,000–$450,000 phase-out); a non-first-time buyer of a new home reading only this page would miss what they still qualify for.

The $835,000 test comes before the house hunt (Nov 1, 2026). At or under that fair market value a qualifying first-time buyer is exempt on the first $500,000 of the price; between $835,000 and $860,000 the exemption is only partial — a $25,000 price band worth up to $8,000, decided before an offer is written, not at closing.

faq.q: Can I combine the Home Buyers' Plan and the FHSA, and how much can I take out?

faq.a: As the page's structured FAQ frames it, the deposit is the money that secures the accepted offer and is at risk once subjects are removed, while the down payment is the buyer's total equity contribution at completion, of which the deposit forms part — the page's "typically around 5%" deposit figure and its timing norm are practitioner copy, not confirmed as stated norms; the verified down-payment tiers are the CMHC tiers in.
faq.q: What is the difference between the deposit and the down payment?

faq.a: A qualifying first-time buyer is exempt on the first $500,000 of the price at a fair market value of $835,000 or less, with a partial exemption between $835,000 and $860,000.
faq.q: How much PTT will I pay, and what does a first-time buyer save?

faq.a: At the general rates: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% on the portion to $2,000,000, 3% above $2,000,000, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000. A qualifying first-time buyer is exempt on the first $500,000 of the price at a fair market value of $835,000 or less, with a partial exemption between $835,000 and $860,000.
faq.q: How much property transfer tax will I pay, and what does a first-time buyer save?

faq.a: On a new build or presale, yes — 5% at completion; resale homes are generally exempt. A qualifying first-time buyer can recover up to $50,000 through the FTHB GST/HST rebate (100% of the GST to $1 million, gradually reduced to $1.5 million, none at $1.5 million or more), and the pre-existing new housing rebate alone returns 36% of the GST to a maximum of $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000.
faq.q: Do I pay GST on a home purchase in BC?

faq.a: 5% on homes of $500,000 or less; 5% on the first $500,000 plus 10% on the portion over $500,000 for homes between $500,000 and $1,499,999; and 20% at $1,500,000 or more. Below 20% down, mortgage loan insurance is required, and CMHC's published premium range is 0.6% to 4.5% of the total mortgage amount.
